text.autoconfig.simplelayers.option.vaul: A rare gap in the Overworld bedrock leads into the Bedrock Vault: quiet halls below the bedrock, enclosed by bedrock, a way out only through its riddles. Off: no new gaps, existing gates do nothing. Default: on.
One in this many new Overworld chunks (0-100000, 0 = none) gets a 2 x 2 gap through the bedrock floor with the Vault Gate at its bottom. Default: 400.
Seconds after the first entry until the inner gate seals behind the players (5-600). Until then it leads back out; once nobody is inside it opens again. Default: 30.
Volume of the quiet, random sounds in the Bedrock Vault in percent (0-100, 0 = silent); a drip or a far chime every 30-90 s. The Ambient slider applies too. Default: 40.

text.autoconfig.simplelayers.title: Simple Layers
text.autoconfig.simplelayers.option.clou: Rising above the entry height in the Overworld leads into the Cloud Sea. Off: the Cloud Sea cannot be reached. Default: on.
Overworld height (400-1000) above which a rising player enters the Cloud Sea; falling out of it returns 20 blocks lower. Default: 700.
Hard mode: mist pits go right through the island. Off: a hidden hollow with a cloud floor lies below each pit. Default: off.
Mist blocks shed a rare falling haze so careful players spot a pit. Default: on.
text.autoconfig.simplelayers.option.back: Entrance shafts and Glitched Bedrock appear in the Overworld; their rifts lead into the Backrooms (Level 0 and the deeper levels). Off: no shafts, plain bedrock, no way in. Default: on.
One new Overworld chunk in this many (4-10000) gets a Glitched Bedrock. Default: 48.
Falling 32 blocks below the Overworld floor lands in the Backrooms instead of the void. Default: off.

Players in any Backrooms level get the Backroom effect: in survival they cannot break the walls, floors and ceilings, and no piston moves them there - only Simple Machines' Netherite Piston breaks them. Supplies (wood, cobwebs, chests) stay breakable. Default: on.
Some Backrooms rooms hold an office (desk, chair, a pile of oak logs, sometimes a crafting table) or cobwebs in the corners, so you can survive and craft. Default: on.
Rare footsteps that come closer behind you and stop; no creature, no damage. Default: off.
One in this many new Overworld chunks (0-100000, 0 = none) gets a fenced-off maintenance shaft whose floor leads into the Backrooms; only on flat, dry ground. Default: 200.
Volume of the quiet, random sounds inside the Backrooms in percent (0-100, 0 = silent); no constant hum, a sound every 20-60 s. The Ambient slider applies too. Default: 50.
block.simplelayers.glitched_bedrock.tool: Only a Netherite Pickaxe breaks it

simplelayers.guide.page.1.title: Simple Layers
simplelayers.guide.page.1: Two new world layers: rise above y 700 of the Overworld into the Cloud Sea, a sky of cloud islands,
simplelayers.guide.page.2.title: Simple Layers
simplelayers.guide.page.2: or break Glitched Bedrock with a Netherite Pickaxe and fall into the Backrooms - endless, empty yellow rooms. Find the exit.
simplelayers.guide.page.3.title: Cloud blocks
simplelayers.guide.page.3: Cloud Block, Cloud Stone and Mist Block break instantly, by hand too.
simplelayers.guide.page.4.title: Cloud blocks
simplelayers.guide.page.4: A Cloud Block takes 30 % off fall damage, Cloud Stone 10 % (a damage factor like the Hay Bale, not a shorter fall). Mist has no collision: you walk and fall through it.
simplelayers.guide.page.5.title: The Cloud Sea
simplelayers.guide.page.5: Rise above y 700 in the Overworld (config clouds.entryY, 400-1000) and you enter the Cloud Sea, a sky dimension of floating islands over the same x/z.
simplelayers.guide.page.6.title: The Cloud Sea
simplelayers.guide.page.6: Fall below its bottom and you come back to the Overworld 20 blocks under the entry height with 3 s of Slow Falling.
simplelayers.guide.page.7.title: The Backrooms
simplelayers.guide.page.7: Two ways lead into the Backrooms:
simplelayers.guide.page.8.title: The Backrooms
simplelayers.guide.page.8: rarely a fenced-off maintenance shaft stands in the Overworld (see "Entrance shaft"), and rarely Glitched Bedrock sits in the bedrock floor (one new chunk in 48, config backrooms.entranceRarity;
simplelayers.guide.page.9.title: The Backrooms
simplelayers.guide.page.9: only a Netherite Pickaxe breaks it, about 30 s, and it leaves a Rift). Whatever falls into a Rift lands in Level 0:
simplelayers.guide.page.10.title: The Backrooms
simplelayers.guide.page.10: endless empty rooms, 8 x 8 blocks and 5 high, with yellow wallpaper, damp carpet and humming neon lights.
simplelayers.guide.page.11.title: The quick way out
simplelayers.guide.page.11: Level 0 always has an exit near you: every block of 12 x 12 rooms has one exit room,
simplelayers.guide.page.12.title: The quick way out
simplelayers.guide.page.12: a free-standing wall with the Exit Door under a green EXIT sign, and from every room a way of at most 18 rooms leads to it.
simplelayers.guide.page.13.title: The quick way out
simplelayers.guide.page.13: In the row and the column of the exit an EXIT sign hangs under the ceiling beside the door that leads on - follow the signs.
simplelayers.guide.page.14.title: The quick way out
simplelayers.guide.page.14: The Exit Door brings you back to the Overworld above the place you came in (with a Backdoor Key 1500-3000 blocks away).
simplelayers.guide.page.15.title: Deeper levels
simplelayers.guide.page.15: Rifts in walls (noclip spots) and Maintenance Doors lead one level deeper; the action bar names the level. Level 1, the Warehouse:
simplelayers.guide.page.16.title: Deeper levels
simplelayers.guide.page.16: a concrete hall 8 high with pillars, racks of crates (wood) and cobwebs (string), supply chests. Level 2, the Pipes: narrow warm corridors under copper ducts, two storeys joined by ladder shafts, many dead ends, chests in some of them.
simplelayers.guide.page.17.title: Deeper levels
simplelayers.guide.page.17: Holes in the floor of both drop into the Poolrooms: calm tiled rooms with shallow and deep pools.
simplelayers.guide.page.18.title: Harder ways out
simplelayers.guide.page.18: In the Pipes every region has a sealed hatch with three valve levers beside it.
simplelayers.guide.page.19.title: Harder ways out
simplelayers.guide.page.19: It opens only when the levers stand right; each try tells you in the action bar how many valves are right, so a little thinking solves it.
simplelayers.guide.page.20.title: Harder ways out
simplelayers.guide.page.20: Behind it lies the Exit Level: bright white corridors, an exit every few rooms, and next to each Exit Door a chest with the reward - always a Backdoor Key, plus diamonds, emeralds, ender pearls or a golden apple.
simplelayers.guide.page.21.title: Harder ways out
simplelayers.guide.page.21: The Poolrooms have exit rooms too, with a smaller reward.
simplelayers.guide.page.22.title: Entrance shaft
simplelayers.guide.page.22: Rarely (one new Overworld chunk in 200, config backrooms.shaftRarity, 0 = none; only on flat, dry ground) a fenced-off maintenance shaft stands in the open:
simplelayers.guide.page.23.title: Entrance shaft
simplelayers.guide.page.23: a concrete pad, a barrier of posts and yellow-and-black Caution Tape, Caution Signs facing out and orange warning lights on the corners, a hoist frame with a chain over a 3 x 3 shaft.
simplelayers.guide.page.24.title: Entrance shaft
simplelayers.guide.page.24: A ladder leads 12 blocks down to a floor of rifts - the way into Level 0. The tape stops walking, not jumping.
simplelayers.guide.page.25.title: Sounds
simplelayers.guide.page.25: The Backrooms have no constant hum. Every 20-60 seconds (in the Exit Level less often) one quiet sound plays somewhere near you:
simplelayers.guide.page.26.title: Sounds
simplelayers.guide.page.26: a buzzing tube, a far door, a drip, steam in the pipes, lapping water in the Poolrooms.
simplelayers.guide.page.27.title: Sounds
simplelayers.guide.page.27: Only you hear it. Config backrooms.ambientVolume (0-100 %, 0 = silent); the Ambient slider of the sound options applies too.
simplelayers.guide.page.28.title: Walls, hull and supplies
simplelayers.guide.page.28: In the Backrooms you carry the Backroom effect (config backrooms.unbreakableWalls): in survival you cannot break the wallpaper, carpet, ceiling tiles and lights, and no piston moves them there.
simplelayers.guide.page.29.title: Walls, hull and supplies
simplelayers.guide.page.29: Only the Netherite Piston (Simple Machines) breaks a wall in front of it.
simplelayers.guide.page.30.title: The Listener
simplelayers.guide.page.30: Option backrooms.listener (off by default): now and then footsteps sound behind you in the Backrooms, come closer and stop. There is no creature and no damage - only the sound.
